title: The ideal of a purely inseparable root is prime and contracts correctly
statement: Let R be an integrally closed domain with fraction field K, and L a field extension of K in prime characteristic p. Suppose every a in L has a^(p^e) in K and R/xR is a domain. Put S = integralClosure R L. For y in S with y^(p^e) = x, the ideal yS is prime and its contraction to R equals xR. No Noetherian or finite-dimensional hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 032P, the equality q = {f in S | f^q in xR} = yS (steps 2-3 of the parent)

proof.text: Every a in S has a^(p^e) in R: use the common-power hypothesis, descend integrality through K -> L, and apply normality in the fraction field.
The map R -> S is injective. If y=0, positivity of p^e forces x=0. The root ideal is the zero prime of the domain S, and injectivity gives its contraction zero.

Otherwise choose a prime J over xR by integral lying over. The equation y^(p^e)=x places y in J. For a in J, write a^(p^e)=r in R; contraction places r in xR, so r=xt. Then (a/y)^(p^e)=t, which makes a/y integral by the monic equation. Thus a=y(a/y) lies in yS. Hence J=yS and its contraction is xR.

lean.statement:
theorem tate_root_ideal_prime
    (R : Type u) (K L : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L]
    (x : R) (hnormal : IsIntegrallyClosed R)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p]
    [IsDomain (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))]
    (e : ℕ) (hpow : ∀ a : L, a ^ (p ^ e) ∈ (algebraMap K L).range)
    (y : integralClosure R L)
    (hy : y ^ (p ^ e) = algebraMap R (integralClosure R L) x) :
    (Ideal.span ({y} : Set (integralClosure R L))).IsPrime ∧
      (Ideal.span ({y} : Set (integralClosure R L))).comap
        (algebraMap R (integralClosure R L)) = Ideal.span ({x} : Set R)
